questions.title: External style sheet
questions.text: Write the HTML that links every page of the site to the style sheet **css/style.css**, and state where in the page it is placed.

scheme.mark_scheme: <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/style.css"> (1); placed in the <head> (1)

points.criterion: link tag with rel and href

scheme.model_answer: <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/style.css"> — inside the <head> element.

questions.title: Why one CSS file
questions.text: Explain **two** advantages of using one external CSS file for all pages of a web application.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): consistent design on every page; change made once updates all pages; less repeated code / smaller HTML files; file cached by the browser → faster loading; content separated from presentation
scheme.model_answer: All pages look the same, and a change to the colours or fonts is made once in one file instead of on every page.

questions.title: Relative links
questions.text: Explain why links between pages of the same site should be **relative** (e.g. `register.php`) rather than absolute (e.g. `https://school.kz/register.php`).

scheme.mark_scheme: Relative links work wherever the site is placed (1); if the site moves to another domain / server / folder or is tested locally the links do not break (1)
scheme.model_answer: Relative links point to files from the current location, so they still work if the whole site is moved to another domain or tested on a local computer.

questions.title: REQUEST_METHOD
questions.text: In register.php the processing starts with `if ($_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] === "POST")`. Explain why.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- The same page shows the form and processes it (1)
- the processing / validation runs only after the form is submitted, so no error messages appear when the page is first opened (1)
scheme.model_answer: The page both shows the form and handles it; the check makes the script process the data only after the user submits it, so error messages are not shown when the empty form first opens.

questions.title: htmlspecialchars
questions.text: Using htmlspecialchars() when displaying a user's name stops HTML or JavaScript typed by the user from running on the page.

scheme.mark_scheme: True.

questions.title: Include files
questions.text: Explain why the header, navigation bar and database connection are kept in separate files that are included on each page.

scheme.mark_scheme: Code is written once and reused (1); a change is made in one place and updates all pages / no duplicated code / fewer errors (1)
scheme.model_answer: They are written once and reused on every page, so changing the menu or the database password means editing only one file.

questions.title: Test plan
questions.text: The grade field accepts values from 7 to 12. Complete a test plan with one normal, one boundary and one erroneous test value and the expected result.

scheme.mark_scheme: Normal: 8–11, accepted (1); Boundary: 7 or 12 accepted (or 6 / 13 rejected, as just outside) (1); Erroneous: e.g. 15 / -3 / "ten", error message (1)
scheme.model_answer:
| Type | Value | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | 10 | Accepted |
| Boundary | 12 | Accepted |
| Erroneous | 15 | "Grade must be 7–12." |

questions.title: Separation of concerns
questions.text: Explain why HTML, CSS and PHP code should be kept in separate files.

scheme.mark_scheme: Easier to read / maintain — each file has one job (1); different people (designer / programmer) can work at the same time / design can change without touching the logic (1)
scheme.model_answer: Each file has one job, so the code is easier to read and maintain, and the design can be changed without touching the PHP logic.

questions.title: Library website interface
questions.text: A school library is building a web application with three pages: **index.php** (catalogue), **search.php** (search books) and **contact.php** (contact the librarian). All pages use the style sheet **library.css**.

scheme.mark_scheme: <title>Library</title> inside head (1); <link rel="stylesheet" href="library.css"> (1)

```html

  <title>Library</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="library.css">
</head>
```

parts.title: Navigation
parts.text: Write HTML for a navigation bar linking the three pages.

scheme.mark_scheme: nav element (1); three <a href> with the correct relative file names (1); link text for each page (1)

parts.title: Consistency
parts.text: Explain why the same navigation bar and style sheet should be used on every page.

scheme.mark_scheme: Consistent interface — users always find the menu in the same place / easy to learn (1); changes made once in shared files (1)
scheme.model_answer: Users always see the menu in the same place with the same design, so the site is easy to use, and changes are made once for all pages.

questions.title: Book request form
questions.text: On contact.php pupils request books. The form sends **pupil** (name), **grade** and several check boxes named **books[]** to request.php using POST. A pupil may request at most **3** books.

parts.title: Form tag
parts.text: Write the opening `<form>` tag and one check box for the book **"The Hobbit"**.

scheme.mark_scheme: <form action="request.php" method="post"> (1); <input type="checkbox" name="books[]" value="The Hobbit"> (1)
scheme.model_answer:
```html
<form action="request.php" method="post">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="books[]" value="The Hobbit"> The Hobbit</label>
```

parts.title: request.php
parts.text:
Write request.php. It must:
- read the three inputs,
- check that the pupil's name is entered and between 1 and 3 books are chosen, outputting an error message otherwise,
- if the data is valid, output "Thank you, <name>" and list the requested books one per line.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- reads pupil, grade, books from $_POST (default empty array) (1)
- presence check on the name (1)
- count of books checked 1–3 (1)
- error messages output (1)
- selection so the thank-you appears only when valid (1)
- loop through the books array (1)
- each book output, user data escaped with htmlspecialchars (1)

parts.title: Client check
parts.text: Write JavaScript that stops the form from being sent if more than 3 books are ticked.

scheme.mark_scheme: Counts the ticked check boxes (querySelectorAll(':checked')) on submit (1); preventDefault() / return false with a message when > 3 (1)

parts.title: Both checks
parts.text: Explain why the number of books is checked both in JavaScript and in request.php.

scheme.mark_scheme: JavaScript gives instant feedback without sending data (1); server check needed because client-side checks can be disabled / bypassed (1)
scheme.model_answer: The JavaScript check warns the pupil immediately, but it can be switched off, so the PHP script must check again before accepting the request.

questions.title: Style and testing
questions.text: The library web developer wants the application to be easy to maintain and reliable.

parts.title: Include
parts.text: The menu is stored in **menu.php** and the database connection in **db.php**. Write the PHP that adds both to search.php.

scheme.mark_scheme: include / require "menu.php"; (1) include / require "db.php"; (1)
scheme.model_answer:
```php
<?php include "menu.php"; include "db.php"; ?>
```

parts.title: Style rules
parts.text: Describe **three** rules of good programming style the developer should follow.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any three (1 each): meaningful names; comments; indentation; constants instead of magic numbers; reuse code with include / functions; separate HTML, CSS and PHP; validate input and handle errors
scheme.model_answer: 1 Use meaningful variable names such as $bookCount. 2 Add comments explaining each part. 3 Use a constant MAX_BOOKS = 3 instead of writing 3 in many places.

parts.title: Testing
parts.text: Complete the test plan for the number of books chosen (allowed 1–3).

scheme.mark_scheme: Normal 2 → accepted (1); Boundary 1 or 3 → accepted (or 0 / 4 rejected) (1); Erroneous e.g. 5 → error message (1)
scheme.model_answer:
| Type | Books | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | 2 | Request accepted |
| Boundary | 3 | Request accepted |
| Erroneous | 5 | Error message |

summary: Building a complete web application step by step — planning the pages and files, creating the interface with semantic HTML and an external CSS file, implementing site navigation, sending form data to a server-side script, processing it with validation, selection and iteration, saving results, reusing code with include, writing in a good programming style and testing the application.

blocks.content: A **web application** is a website whose pages **do something** with the user's data: register for events, place orders, show search results. It combines **HTML** (content and structure), **CSS** (presentation), **client-side JavaScript** (interactivity) and a **server-side script** such as **PHP** (processing and storing data, often in a **database**).

items.title: Steps of development
items.content:
- **Analyse** what the users need and list the pages.
- **Design** the layout (wireframe), navigation and forms.
- **Build** the HTML structure and the CSS style sheet.
- **Program** the scripts that process the data.
- **Test** with normal, boundary and erroneous data; fix errors.
- **Publish** the site on a web server.

items.title: Separation of concerns
items.content:
- **HTML** — what is on the page.
- **CSS** — how it looks.
- **JavaScript** — how it reacts in the browser.
- **PHP** — what happens on the server.
Keeping them in separate files makes the application easier to **maintain**.

blocks.content:
- Use `htmlspecialchars()` when displaying user input, so that a user cannot inject HTML or JavaScript into the page (**XSS**).
- Use **prepared statements** for database queries (prevents **SQL injection**).
- Repeat every check on the **server** — client-side checks can be switched off.

items.title: Style rules in a project
items.content:
- Separate **content (HTML)**, **style (CSS file)** and **logic (PHP / JS)**.
- Put repeated code (header, navigation, database connection) in **one file** and `include` it on each page.
- **Meaningful names**, comments, indentation, **constants** instead of magic numbers.
- **Validate** all input and handle errors with clear messages.

items.title: Why it matters
items.content:
- Several people can work on the site at the same time.
- A change to the menu or the colours is made **once**.
- Errors are easier to find and fix; the code is easier to extend.

[2]** All pages are styled from **one file**, so the design is **consistent** (1) and a change is made **once** for the whole site (1). **Q: Write PHP that outputs "Free" if the number of events is 0, otherwise the fee of 700 per event. [3]** `if (count($events) == 0)` (1) `echo "Free";` `else echo 700 * count($events);` (1 calculation, 1 output). **Q: Explain why include files are used for the header and the menu. - Forgetting `name` attributes, or `[]` for check boxes that should arrive as an array.
- Using absolute links for pages of the same site — the links break when the site moves.
- Processing the form before checking `REQUEST_METHOD` — errors appear when the page is first opened.
- Copying the same header into every file instead of using `include`.
